citations.claim: initial total energy before any integration
speed grows far faster than g*dt allows, showing spurious energy injection while in free fall with no contacts or controller
first energy_bound violation: energy exceeds E0 plus tolerance with zero controller work

counterfactual.change: Reduced dt from 0.031889596040442662 to 0.001 (one field) to leave the fast-body substep regime; same 2 steps, no violation.

explanation: Single body in free fall (no walls, no contacts, controller disabled) gains ~78-80 J per step: vy goes -48.80 -> -50.68 -> -52.55, i.e. ~1.88 m/s per dt=0.0319s step, ~6x the analytic g*dt=0.31 m/s. inspect_state reports 54-56 substeps_in_step for these fast steps, so the fast-path substep loop over-applies gravity (adds far too much velocity) while position advance stays consistent with the inflated velocity, injecting kinetic energy with zero controller work and breaking energy_bound. Using dt=0.001 (no large-substep regime) conserves energy, confirming the large-dt substep integration as cause.
vision_note: The single blue ball falls an extremely large distance in just two steps, dropping from near the top toward the lower part of the arena. It also drifts rightward as it falls, with no walls, other bodies, or waypoints visible.
